name: North Dakota
overview: North Dakota does not sell tax liens to investors. When property taxes have been delinquent for two or more years, the county auditor gives notice of foreclosure of the tax lien by June 1, and the lien is foreclosed on October 1. The county then takes a tax deed and sells the property at its own public auction, held each year in November in the counties covered here, with each parcel sold separately to the highest bidder but not below a minimum sale price. Under state law, some cities have the first option to buy, so parcels on a county's list may be gone by sale day. In Burleigh County the former owner can still stop the sale by paying everything owed before the auction starts.

overview_sources.quote: On or before June first in each year, the county auditor shall give notice of foreclosure of tax lien for all property for which two or more years have passed since the tax became due.
The tax lien foreclosure date is October first after the service of the notice of foreclosure.
EACH PARCEL of real estate will be offered separately and sold to the highest bidder thereof, but not for a sum less than the minimum sale price.
ACCORDING TO NDCC 57-28-19, some Cities have the first option to purchase property; therefore, some parcels may not be listed at sale time.

counties.how_to_bid: Bid in person at the annual sale in the Cass County Commission Room. Each parcel goes to the highest bidder at or above the posted minimum price, and payment is cash or check, deposited at once with the Finance Office. Anyone who owes delinquent taxes in any North Dakota county can't be the high bidder. The county issues a county deed, and the former owner can redeem until the sale.
